newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Hong Leong Finance sees levelling growth.
newsitem.headline: Hong Leong Finance sees levelling growth.

text.p: Hong Leong Finance Ltd said on Friday it sees a levelling of profit growth in 1997, although it was cautiously optimistic about prospects.

Chairman Kwek Leng Beng said in Hong Leong's report on its 1996 results that the "outlook for 1997 is cautiously optimistic with growth in the Singapore economy forecast to remain within five to seven percent.
"In line with this, a levelling of profit growth for the Group is to be expected."
Hong Leong reported 14.8 percent growth in net profits in 1996, to Singapore $87.39 million.
Kwek said in 1997: "Competition for business will continue to remain aggressive and the property and car markets are likely to consolidate further."
He said the group would continue to focus on broadening activities by searching out new profitable niches, building up quality loan assets and controlling costs.
"Barring unforeseen circumstances, the directors expect the group to turn in a set of satisfactory results in 1997," Kwek said.
